The two accent edges B–D and C–D are the minimum edge cut separating B from E, and the card returns them as the set of pairs (B, D) and (C, D)." width="100%"} Returns the set of edges whose removal disconnects the source from the sink. Uses the max-flow min-cut theorem via Ford-Fulkerson algorithm to identify the minimum cut. By default every edge has capacity `1` (edge weights are ignored), so the result is a smallest set of edges by count, and its size equals `minimum_cut_value()`. With `capacity=` it is a set of edges of least total capacity instead: the edges running from the source side to the sink side of `minimum_cut()`'s partition. For undirected graphs, edges are treated as bidirectional. For directed graphs, only forward edges are considered: the cut consists of edges pointing from the source side to the sink side. Where `minimum_cut_value()` reports *how many* edges must be removed, this method reports *which* ones. It is useful for: - finding the critical links between two sites in a communication or transport network - deciding where adding a single link would most improve redundancy - splitting a graph into two parts with as few broken connections as possible When several minimum cuts exist, only one of them is returned; in practice it is the cut closest to `source=`. If the sink is already unreachable, the result is an empty set. The method does not modify the graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node on the source side of the cut, given as an integer node ID or a string label. [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node on the sink side of the cut, given as an integer node ID or a string label. Must be a different node than `source=`. [capacity]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of an edge attribute to use as capacity, as in `minimum_cut_value()`. If `None` (default), every edge has capacity `1`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [set[tuple[int, int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Set of `(source_id, target_id)` tuples identifying the cut edges by their endpoint node IDs, in the orientation the edges were stored with. Parallel edges between the same two nodes appear as a single tuple. Empty if `target=` is unreachable from `source=`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If source or sink node doesn't exist, if they're the same, or if an edge lacks the attribute named by `capacity=`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In this 4-cycle, `A` reaches `C` along two separate 2-edge paths, so breaking that connection requires removing one edge from each path: ::: {#95e05720 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("A", "D")], auto_create_nodes=True) ) cut_edges = graph.minimum_edge_cut("A", "C") sorted( (graph.get_label_from_id(u), graph.get_label_from_id(v)) for u, v in cut_edges ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [('A', 'B'), ('A', 'D')] ``` ::: ::: The same approach identifies critical links in a directed network. Two parallel routers between `Router1` and `Server2` provide redundancy there, but the single link from `Server1` into `Router1` is still a bottleneck: ::: {#55f0899a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_edges( [ ("Server1", "Router1"), ("Router1", "Router2"), ("Router2", "Server2"), ("Router1", "Router3"), ("Router3", "Server2"), ], auto_create_nodes=True, ) ) critical_links = graph.minimum_edge_cut("Server1", "Server2") [ (graph.get_label_from_id(u), graph.get_label_from_id(v)) for u, v in critical_links ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [('Server1', 'Router1')] ``` ::: :::
